title: STEM-iDPC Imaging for Resolving Atomic Structural Features of Stacking Faults and Domain Connections in the Li- and Mn-rich Cathode
content: The imaging technique of scanning transmission electron microscopy – integrated differential phase contrast (STEM-iDPC) has been emerging as a powerful tool for studying materials composed of both heavy and light ions such as oxides [1,2]. Different from the commonly used imaging techniques, where a contrast roughly proportional to Z2 (Z is the atomic number) by STEM-high-angle annular dark field (HAADF), a diffraction contrast by STEM-annular dark field (ADF) and a phase contrast in STEM-bright field (BF) and high resolution TEM (HRTEM), STEM-iDPC is able to capture heavy and light atomic columns simultaneously based on a more straightforward interpretable linear Z contrast [3,4]. Therefore, the projection of the entire structure can be imaged, which provides the possibility to get more insightful microstructural information.
